question: ||(mlx_img.mean(0) - mu_img) @ Wi_v2.T|| — did jitter training make v2 relatively more sensitive to the real displacement direction
conclusion: Reader's conclusion CONFIRMED in direction, modestly overestimated in magnitude (219/1.293 vs predicted 251/1.49). Jitter suppressed random directions 3.00x in rho but the real direction only 1.47x; the real/random excitation ratio crossed 1.0 (0.635 -> 1.293), i.e., the real displacement now excites v2 MORE than a random direction of equal norm. v2 still beats v1 against the real displacement in absolute rho (0.909 vs 1.339) which is why the end-task gain is +4.6 not +38, but the mechanism is scale plus preferential armoring of directions that do not occur. Random-jitter augmentation is the wrong prior for structured runtime drift.
